reasons: REGIME VIOLATION (state_only): build_feedback calls harness_lib.best_query(view) and tells the model which query to ask next, written as a ready-to-copy <query> tag with the label 'Most informative next query'. The state_only regime forbids ranking or recommending queries.

REGIME VIOLATION (state_only): the feedback also gives the split count for the recommended query ('{n - ones} of the {n} give 0, {ones} give 1'). That is a per-query information value, which state_only explicitly forbids.

The whole hypothesis is to hand the model the single max-entropy action. Without query recommendation nothing is left of the mechanism, so a small edit cannot make this candidate compliant. It belongs to the open regime only.
risk_notes: No instance leakage seen: nothing is hard-coded per instance. LABELS='ABCDEFGH' and the bit formatting depend only on view.c and view.k.
No file, network or truth access. Everything comes from view.H, view.alive, view.k and view.c, which are public state.

final_hint gives a full <guess> string built from view.H[view.alive[0]]. That is derived from public state and would be allowed on its own, but when more than one configuration remains it hands over an arbitrary one with no caveat about which.
When n <= 1 the fixed filler query _qtag(view, 0) is harmless, but it still asks the model to spend a query. If budget use is scored, ending early would be cleaner.

The docstring claims seed results (29%/76% repeat rates, 96% for a canonical scan, 4 of 53 exact). These are claims about the selection instances and could not be checked here. Treat them as possible selection-set tuning if the candidate is resubmitted under the open regime.
The parent oracle_hint also calls best_query, so it would fail this same state_only screen. It should not be used as a state_only baseline.
